about.title:
HELLO THERE
I'M SHANTANU
about.subtitle: Generalist Game Programmer
paragraphs: I taught myself game development from YouTube tutorials, especially Brackeys, to build my final year B.Tech project as I wanted it to be special. It combined mechanics from my 3 all time favourite games Halo, Portal, and Dark Souls.

Working professionally as a game developer has completely changed how I look at and play video games. Now, every time I see an interesting mechanic, I immediately try to break down how it was built in my head.
I like playing games from varied genres. My first ever game was DOOM 1993 and some of my recent favourites are Baldur's Gate 3, Hi Fi Rush, and TABS, all of which are very unique and entertaining.

experience.title: Game Programmer | Parody Studios
bullets: Independently completed and released two multiplayer titles; built robust systems around core mechanics including game modes, server-side validation, and admin panels.
Implemented secure backend pipelines using Firebase and PlayFab; engineered custom matchmaking logic via User IDs and synced complete player states.
Spearheaded R&D on Animation Rigging for procedural animations, integrating them into production builds.
Collaborated with art teams to implement ragdoll physics, custom shaders, and responsive UI animations.

education: B.Tech in Electronics & Communication Engineering | IIIT Pune

projects.title: Caro Premier League (CPL)
projects.tag: Multiplayer & LiveOps | Low End Optimisation | Web3 & Firebase | Anti-Cheat | OneSignal
projects.description: Commercial multiplayer cricket title released on Android and iOS featuring serverless tournaments, custom Web3 authentication, and a LiveOps admin dashboard.

rows.text: Full stack development: joined in early stages as sole programmer, driving a dual store release and LiveOps maintenance.
Fixed gameplay loop desyncs: driven by the authoritative hit event instead of local swing timing on the receiving client.
Integrated REST APIs for marketplace inventory management and in game token transactions and trades.
Eliminated credential desyncs: created custom Firebase JWTs via Cloud Functions tied directly to immutable wallet IDs.
Dynamic reward splitting: algorithm calculates balance limits and splits payouts across multiple NFTs in a single API payload.
Scheduled matchmaking: queues open at fixed minute marks and survive app restarts via timestamps, with roster validation and local push reminders.
Built tutorials and AI bots inside an online-only architecture, alongside friend-code lobbies and live player challenges.
Serverless tournaments: Firebase Cloud Functions and OneSignal push alerts pair players and advance brackets without a dedicated server.
Built LiveOps Admin Dashboard allowing the team to manage game modes, moderate accounts, audit token flows, and send OneSignal API push notifications.
Prevented multi account NFT farming: logged daily asset usage to database nodes, cross referencing hashsets post match to block traded assets from claiming twice.
Hardened client integrity using Anti-Cheat Toolkit (ACTk) memory obfuscation, hack detections, and forced startup version and ban-status gates.
Created a runtime character swapper: unified the roster onto a single animated rig, scripting face and kit swaps to cut animation workload by 90%+.
Multi language Audio Manager: supports localised commentary swapping from settings with sequential non repeating dialogue queues.
Integrated native OS features: implemented gallery based profile picture uploads and a referral system that caches runtime win screen screenshots to temp storage for native OS sharing.
Cut build footprint by 80%+ (1+ GB APK to 170 MB APK) through tier based texture, mesh, audio, and keyframe compression.
Cut daily bandwidth from 2+ GBs to under 100 MB for around 30 daily users using local snapshot caching, shallow REST queries, and database schema restructuring.
Reduced UI rendering overhead by packing relevant sprite sheets and isolating HUD elements in nested canvases, eliminating redundant layout rebuilds.
Secured dual store certification: navigated Apple and Google policy guidelines to publish a tokenised external asset game.
Authored technical GDD and handover docs to transition the project to external developers and QA testers.

projects.title: Team Based Multiplayer Hand Cricket
projects.tag: Team Multiplayer | Cross Platform | Unity Netcode | Lobby & Relay | 34 MB APK
projects.description: Cross-platform up to 5v5 multiplayer adaptation of the real-life hand cricket game built for Android and WebGL, featuring lightweight netcode and a compact build size.

rows.text: Simultaneous reveal multiplayer: an up to 5v5 adaptation of the classic childhood hand game, playable instantly in your browser (landscape) with open-source network logic.
34 MB APK with just 11 MB of raw assets (including a 6 MB OST) built from scratch.
Fixed silent WebGL failures: multithreaded network flows that worked in the Editor and on Android failed silently in browsers, requiring a complete refactor into Coroutines and void RPCs.
Handled mid match disconnects: custom index-shifting recalculates batting and bowling orders on the fly, with host drop fallbacks.
Android and WebGL crossplay allows instant browser access across any device without requiring an install.
Dynamic transport switching between DTLS on mobile and WebSockets on WebGL at startup via Unity Relay.
Minimised network bandwidth by syncing only player ID lists and team names via persistent NetworkVariables.
Lightweight event driven architecture uses zero NetworkTransforms, executing all 3D movements and animations deterministically on the client.
Zero heartbeat pings: host deletes the lobby on launch, recreates a new one post-match, and distributes the new lobby code via Relay.
TV broadcast-style match HUD: built a dynamic UI overlay to display real time team scoreboards and match states similar to recent World Cups.
Interactive 3D menu model: avatars physically sit inside a school classroom, dynamically swapping seats and positions to reflect their current match roles.
Hundreds of avatar combinations generated from a minimal 3-face, 3-hat asset pack using an HSV colour slider.

projects.title: Super Over Cricket
projects.tag: PlayFab & Firebase | Low End Optimisation | Release Management | LiveOps Tuning | Facebook SDK
projects.description: Commercial 1v1 multiplayer cricket title on Android featuring skill-based matchmaking, Facebook cloud saves and backup, and remote LiveOps physics tuning with 30k+ downloads.

rows.text: 30k+ downloads: took over late stage production as sole programmer to complete social systems, UI/UX, matchmaking, release, and maintenance.
Resolved high-latency state desyncs: bypassed local batting emulation on the receiving client, syncing match state strictly on authoritative delivery outcomes.
Solved store submission restriction: completed 3 months of post-launch maintenance over remote macOS screen share to clear Google compromised-account compliance flags.
Skill based matchmaking (PlayFab): the search range widens over time, then routes to a bot match when the timer expires.
Interactive tutorial onboards new players into timing-based batting and bowling mechanics before entering live queues.
Facebook SDK integration handles cross-install cloud saves, profile syncing, guest fallbacks, and compliant user data deletion.
Firebase friend system links Facebook friends and recent friend-battle opponents, auto-detects a copied room code, and offers to paste it.
Remote physics tuning: WebGL Firebase Admin Panel adjusts live ball speed and spin values without client patches.
Unix timestamp-ordered match histories stored and queried via strict Firebase Security Rules.
70 MB download size: compressed 3D stadium assets, audio files, and textures to optimise for low-end devices, maintaining around 200 MB installed footprint.

projects.title: Interactive Web Portfolio
projects.tag: 5 MB Initial Load | Data Driven UI | UI Toolkit | JS Bridge
projects.description: An interactive portfolio built entirely in Unity UI Toolkit for WebGL, featuring a cyberpunk aesthetic, JSON driven case studies, and custom swipe navigation.

rows.text: Around 5 MB first-load download: a Unity UI Toolkit portfolio built and deployed solo, featuring a cyberpunk aesthetic with background shaders and UI glitch effects.

OS-level inertia filtering: operating systems mask raw trackpad input with synthetic momentum. Wrote a 'Decay Gravity Well' algorithm in JavaScript to filter out lingering inertia tails and isolate deliberate swipes.

Overcame UI Toolkit limitations: bypassed the lack of native CSS @media queries by writing a custom C# resize observer that evaluates viewport geometry at runtime to toggle an .is-mobile class, avoiding duplicate UI trees.

JSON driven case studies: dynamically spawns UXML project cards and media rows using local StreamingAssets JSON and remote server media, bypassing WebGL memory constraints and allowing instant content updates without rebuilding.

Single instance video streaming: routed all case study media through a single recycled VideoPlayer, streaming clips dynamically on demand rather than downloading them to drastically reduce RAM overhead and user bandwidth.

Unified input normalisation: a custom .jslib intercepts disparate browser events (trackpad deltas, touch coordinates, and browser back-buttons), blocking default browser animations and routing them into a single deterministic Unity state machine.
History API sync: appends virtual anchors to the URL via 'history.pushState', binding the custom swipe gestures and browser back/forward actions directly to Unity UI transitions.

Custom HTML template: authored a responsive WebGL wrapper that caps devicePixelRatio at 1.5x to maintain frame rates on high-DPI displays, configuring server headers for Brotli (.br) binary compression.
Cached element references resolved once at startup avoid per frame visual-tree queries.

projects.title: Finquest
projects.tag: 7.5 MB Initial Load | ScriptableObject | Educational | JS Bridge | DOTween
projects.description: A gamified WebGL educational experience developed in around 2 weeks to serve as the interactive playable pitch for a finance learning kids app.

rows.text: Rapid 2 week production cycle: prototyped, programmed, and shipped a complete demo WebGL title in around two weeks for a group project.
Custom WebGL wrapper: authored a responsive HTML template utilising 100dvh and dynamic meta tags to ensure consistent viewport scaling and prevent mobile URL bars from clipping the canvas.
External app integration: exposed the Unity instance globally through the Web template, establishing a two way JavaScript bridge to support embedding the game inside Flutter WebViews and web apps.

Data-driven progression: decoupled content from logic using hierarchical ScriptableObjects, allowing instant iteration of level data, UI assets, and dictionary definitions without altering the codebase.
Dynamic mini-game routing: implemented bitmasking to tag question ScriptableObjects with compatible game types, randomly routing questions into one of four distinct types at runtime.
Math driven input systems: built Tinder style swiping and drag and drop sorting by evaluating screen-space deltas and RectTransform overlaps, bypassing Unity's 2D physics engine.
Single-scene architecture: eliminated browser lag spikes and scene load hitching by preloading all mini games into cached CanvasGroups, toggling states via alpha and raycast blocking.
7.5 MB initial load: achieved a highly compact WebGL footprint by aggressively stripping unused engine code and compressing all project assets down to around 2 MB.
Pooled spawning: utilised object pooling for rapidly spawning elements to minimise garbage collection (GC) stutters in the browser.
Code driven UI animation: replaced Unity Animator clips with scalable DOTween sequences for all UI animations including staggered UI spawns, drag-and-tilt mechanics, and immediate player feedback.

projects.title: Boss Fight Prototype
projects.tag: State Machines | Physics Layers | Combat AI
projects.description: A 2D combat prototype featuring a multi-phase boss, distance-based AI behaviour, and responsive i-frame dodge mechanics.

rows.text: Action RPG combat loop: engineered a complete 2D boss battle with dynamic phase transitions, distinct attack patterns, and a custom player controller.
Distance-based AI: a custom state machine reads player proximity and verticality to switch between ranged artillery, gap-closing leaps, grabs, and anti-air uppercuts.

I-frame & collision manipulation: implemented player dodge sliding and invincible boss sweeps by dynamically swapping physics layers at runtime, bypassing hitboxes without frame-by-frame collider toggling.
Custom knockback and state locks: handle directional explosions and mid-air stuns (dizzy juggling).
Cinematic grab attack: locks the player's transform to the boss's hand.
Animation driven logic: utilised Unity's StateMachineBehaviours and Animation Events to synchronise melee hitboxes, sound effects, and projectile spawning with the visual frames of the attack.
